thread:
sanjay: heads-up — we saw a weird KV memory growth pattern on Qwen-32b when running long-context chat streams (>= 50k tokens). eviction rates spike intermittently and pages never fully compact, causing sustained memory climb across the pod.
anya: ouch. repro on dedicated or hosted? any repro repo/command?
mike: repro on dedicated G5 for us. ran a 12h load with mixed llm variants (llama-2-13b MQA, mistral-7b, qwen-32b). the qwen instances show linear mem growth; others stable.
sanjay: exact repro: run loadbench with prefix-heavy prompts (lots of long histories + embeddings routes) at p95 latency target. command: `./tools/loadbench --model qwen-32b --context 60000 --qps 4 --prefix-reuse 0.8`
lina: saw related rope-scaling weirdness earlier — rope multiplier mismatch makes token positions map to different page slots. can you paste profiler slice?
mike: pasted a small snapshot of the profiler (trimmed):
```
KV pages: 12456 -> 14678 (+18%)
eviction_ops/min: 132 -> 412
avg_page_residency_ms: 4200
page_fragmentation_index: 0.62
kernel_fallbacks: aten->custom_kernel (10% of steps)
batch_fill_ratio: 0.46
```
anya: kernel_fallbacks are scary. if runtime picks a non-optimal kernel frequently, that could increase memory churn due to different prefetch and page usage patterns. any recent kernel-selection change?
ricardo: yes — last week we landed a heuristic to prefer MQA-friendly kernels for llama paths; heuristic had a side-effect: it groups code paths by sequence-length bucketing and that changed our KV page alignments for models with mixed GQA/MQA segments. might be related.
sanjay: note: Qwen uses per-layer kv packing that interacts with rope scaling, so when rope scaling code path triggers (longer pos enc ranges), page layout shifts. combined with the kernel grouping change, we might be thrashing mappings.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-174760 — "qwen kv memory climb under long context load" (sev3). assignee: mike.
mike: quick check: disabling the kernel-grouping flag removes the linear growth in 30m smoke. turned it off on a canary — memory flattened. so it's most likely interaction between kernel selection and kv layout.
anya: interesting. could be two things: 1) kernel selection changes memory access stride causing more fragmentation; 2) batching heuristics changed ordering so prefix reuse doesn't hit cached KV pages as expected.
lina: i ran heap diff — fragmentation hotspots map to layers 10-18 and 30-34 (attention-heavy). Qwen shows repeated small-page allocations that never coalesce. sample map: `page # 0x7f..: owner=layer12 slot=3 len=4k status=stale` repeated.
ricardo: i can try a patch that forces kernel selection to respect existing kv-layout affinity when sequence length changes. should be low risk.
sanjay: action items:
- mike: run 2h canary with kernel-grouping off + stress harness and upload raw slices (logs + perf counters).
- ricardo: prototype a kernel-affinity flag to prefer kernels that preserve kv page stride; add feature-flag gated.
- anya: add a KV page fragmentation metric to telemetry (per-model, per-layer) and emit delta when kernel-selection switches.
- lina: bisect exact layer patterns and produce small repro clip (<=10k tokens) that still triggers the fragmentation so we can unit-test.
mike: doing canary now, will post results in this thread. :thumbsup:
sanjay: thanks. logging note — include `KV_PAGE_ID` and `SEQ_BUCKET` in traces so we can correlate per-request. also add `kernel_hint` to traces.
ops-bot: note: added telemetry ticket TKT-1229 for page fragmentation metric.
mike: canary update (1747601289): with kernel-grouping off, 90m run stable. attaching short trace snippet below.
```
[1747601289] trace: req=abcd1234 model=qwen-32b seq_len=61234 KV_PAGE_HITS=0.83 FRAG_IDX=0.18 kernel_hint=aten
```
anya: great. this lines up. we should still validate ricardo's affinity patch does not regress MQA llms.
ricardo: will run combo smoke across llama/mistral/qwen before flag rollout. ETA EOD.
sanjay: if affinity patch looks good, we can ship as opt-in for now and enable telemetry alerts to catch regressions. thanks everyone.
-- end of thread --
